summary: Reviewed static serving, DOM rendering, role handling and secrets in public/. Probed live server: traversal variants all 404, CSP/nosniff/XFO headers present, no innerHTML anywhere. No blocking findings.

criteria.description: Static serving resists path traversal and exposes no dotfiles or listings
Security headers/CSP (script-src self, no inline) on responses
Untrusted model/user text rendered safely (no HTML injection sinks)
UI role handling is not the sole authorization; no secrets in client

findings.title: Viewer route guard is client-side only
findings.detail: app.js redirects viewers away from #/incidents; this is UX only. Server-side role enforcement was not in scope here and should be confirmed by the API review/verification gate.
findings.recommendation: Ensure API tests cover viewer 403 on incident endpoints.

findings.title: CSRF token held in JS memory, not storage
findings.detail: Token is kept in a module variable and re-fetched via /api/me on load; no localStorage/sessionStorage use. Good. Session cookie is HttpOnly (src/http/cookies.js).

findings.title: Static assets use no-cache (acceptable)
findings.detail: Static assets use no-cache and contain no secrets; API responses use no-store (observed on /api/me 401). Browser journey test not re-run by me.
